text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonia to start negotiations with the London club of creditors in New York about the settlement of the Macedonian debt worth $500 million dollars.

- The World Health Organisation and the U.S. ambassador to Macedonia informed about the latest events in Tetovo, Macedonian health minister Ilija Filipce said. Macedonia expects the arrival of U.S. NATO toxicologists to investigate the poisioning of Albanian schoolchildren in the Tetovo region.
- Obligatory polio vaccination of children aged three months to 18 years will start on October 21. UNICEF has provided 700,000 vaccines.

- Symptoms of poisoning in Tetovo are calming down but ethnic tensions are growing, commentary. Medical personnel in Tetovo hospital is being insulted and threatened, several beds windows and doors of the hospital were demolished by angry relatives of ill children.

- Albania worried over massive poisoning of only Albanian children in Macedonia which "clearly indicates Macedonian anti-Albanian strategy". "These events are not in favor of the development of relations between Macedonia and Albania".

- Macedonian parliamentarians protested because they had not ratified the agreement on trade cooperation with Yugoslavia while it has already gone into effect. "This is a violation of the country's constitutional system" several members of parliament said.

- The PDP party demands postponement of the ratification of the European Charter on national minority rights in the Macedonian parliament. PDP demands change of the articles on the use of minority languages in education, administration and courts.
